extra: map 0: its tile layer, one byte a square, 64 rows of 64, unpacked from T35/L13 by enter_map ($25BD)

comments.text: Class layer, rows 0-31 of 64x64: a nibble a square, even column in the high nibble (map_class_at $0953). Squares by class: 0: 939, 1: 6, 2: 68, 4: 2, 6: 795, 10: 12, 11: 226.
Class layer, rows 32-63 of 64x64: a nibble a square, even column in the high nibble (map_class_at $0953). Squares by class: 0: 1050, 1: 11, 2: 95, 6: 551, 9: 36, 10: 17, 11: 284, 12: 4.

The classes of squares (18, 45) and (19, 45), high and low nibble. Game `$B4F0` `bit $39A9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$39` the code enters at `$B4F1`. On choose_attack's path through the LDA #$50 at $B4EE (api_is_ranged_class at $B4E4 returning carry clear and weapon_rounds at $B4E9 returning 0) the BIT does execute and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N and Z by LDA #$92 at $1DC4, V by the ADC at $28E5, both on game_msg's path), so its value never matters.
Number layer, rows 0-15: one byte a square, the entry of its class's list that holds the square's record (map_number_row $098E, action_record $09B8).

The number of square (41, 2). Game `$81DE` `bit $3CA9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$3C` the code enters at `$81DF`. On melee_monster_attacks's path for a target member whose order is not 5 (from the LDA #$28 at $81D9 or the LDA #$32 at $81DC) the BIT does execute and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N and Z by LDX #$00 at $81E1, V by the ADC at $07D5 in num2_add, through melee_chance), so its value never matters.

The number of square (41, 6). Game `$8DB8` `bit $3DA9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$3D` the code enters at `$8DB9`. On msg_nothing_special's path (its LDA #$26 at $8DB6, called from $8C40 and reached from $8DB4) the BIT does execute and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N, V and Z by the BIT at $8DBB), so its value never matters.
Number layer, rows 16-31: one byte a square, the entry of its class's list that holds the square's record (map_number_row $098E, action_record $09B8).

Game `$B75A` `bit $42A9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$42` the code enters at `$B75B`. Number layer, rows 32-47: one byte a square, the entry of its class's list that holds the square's record (map_number_row $098E, action_record $09B8).

Map code entry 0 (action 0): swaps the pictures of two tiles of the world's tile set, the tile numbers in the square's record bytes +3 and +4: their 32 bitmap bytes at $D000 + 32*tile (addresses from $505A) and their 4 colour bytes at $DC00 + 4*tile (from $5042), exchanged by $5031 with all RAM banked in ($04FC/$04FF), the set lying under the I/O area. Returns carry clear, so the game does not redraw ($8872). Class-6 squares 4 and 5 run it; both records ($4D83, $4D88) name tiles 7 and 86. Tile 7 is the marker the game draws on the party's square ($AF1D), tile 86 the broken jeep at (29,41). That square is check square 0 ("You see a broken down jeep."); its success ("Ace fixes the jeep and you're on your way.") makes it class 6 number 4, so from then on the party is drawn as the jeep, and the square becomes remote change 0 ($4EDD). That one turns (29,40)-(29,32) into exits one square north, (29,31)-(27,31) into exits one square west and (26,31) into class 6 number 5, and the jeep drives itself there: this routine swaps the tiles back and the square becomes exit 21, to map 34 (Needles, the police and gas stations) at column 1, row 17.
